newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian rightists join forces to oust Berisha.
newsitem.headline: Albanian rightists join forces to oust Berisha.

text.p: Albanian rightist parties joined forces on Thursday in a bid to oust President Sali Berisha and prevent ex-communists from winning special general elections set for June 29.

Six rightist parties, the National Front, Demo-Christian Union Party, Movement for Democracy, Conservative Party, Republican Party and the Right Democratic Party, declared they had set up the Albanian United Right (AUR).

"We are convinced that through free and rightful elections we will stop the advancing of the left-wing parties and the autocracy of President Sali Berisha's Democratic Party," Abaz Ermenji, National Front Party chairman, told a news conference.

Ermenji, who was forced to leave the Balkan country when communist dictator Enver Hoxha came to power in 1944, said the grouping would work to end the crisis in Albania and to guarantee stability, social peace and stable government.

"AUR is not only an electoral alliance but also a long-term political coalition able to fulfil the electoral programme and bring stability to the country," Republican Party leader Sabri Godo, flanking Ermenji, said.
The formation of the alliance is seen as a tit-for-tat response to Berisha's efforts to bring together right-wing groups to boost his own Democrats' slim chances of success.
It is also directed at the Socialist Party, the reformed heirs of the communists, who were the historic rivals of rightist and nationalist parties since World War Two.

"People will vote for the Socialist Party because they want a normal Albania for all Albanians," party chairman Fatos Nano told a rally of 20,000 people packed into a soccer stadium in Tirana early this week.

The early elections, brokered by OSCE special envoy Franz Vranitzky, are viewed as a crucial element in defusing tension and building confidence in democracy after the riots sparked by thousands of people losing their savings in dubious pyramid investment schemes.
